After this point, up to 90 percent of the treated wastewater will be routed to the EBDA pipeline for dechlorination and subsequent discharge through a deepwater outfall in to Lower San Francisco Bay.

To improve nitrogen removal, the remaining wastewater (0.95 MGD ), regulated by this Order, will be dechlorinated and routed through an enclosed nitrification system, consisting of membrane aerated biofilm reactors, with an expected nitrification efficiency of at least 75 percent.

To improve nitrogen removal, the remaining wastewater (0.95 MGD ), regulated by this Order, will be dechlorinated and routed through an enclosed nitrification system, consisting of membrane aerated biofilm reactors, with an expected nitrification efficiency of at least 75 percent.

The nitrified wastewater will then be distributed to the top of terraced denitrification bioreactors, consisting of a series of woodchip -filled crates underneath vegetated slopes that will provide a carbon -rich anoxic zone suitable for denitrification.

The wastewater will trickle downward into a shallow ( approximately 24 inches deep ), 6.9-acre, lined and mostly unvegetated open -water wetland that will allow photolysis (light-induced decomposition) of trace organic contaminants (e.g., pesticides and pharmaceuticals). The wetland will also provide additional denitrification as the wastewater flows through interior vegetated dikes equipped with more woodchip -filled crates.
